key_insight: Diffusion transformers can generate and use their own semantic features as internal guidance, removing the need for external pretrained networks while preserving the training acceleration benefits.
problem_solved: Eliminates dependence on external semantic feature extractors (e.g., DINO) that add complexity and brittle dependencies to accelerated DiT training, enabling faster, simpler, and more flexible model training.
method: Extract semantic signals from intermediate DiT representations (attention maps / feature tokens) and treat them as internal guidance targets.
Introduce a lightweight self-guidance objective (auxiliary loss / self-distillation) that aligns diffusion model features across timesteps or snapshots to bootstrap semantic learning.
Integrate the self-guidance objective into standard DiT training to accelerate convergence without needing pretrained external networks.
impact: Makes accelerated DiT training more self-contained and reproducible, lowering engineering overhead and improving adaptability to new domains or modalities while keeping training fast.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: (a) external-guidance setup with a pretrained network feeding features vs (b) Self-Transcendence using internal features as guidance.
Convergence plot: training loss or FID vs epochs showing faster convergence with self-guidance compared to baseline without guidance and external-guidance.
Attention / feature-map montage: example intermediate DiT attention maps or token features used as semantic signals to illustrate what the model uses for self-guidance.
Flowchart of the auxiliary loss: how internal features are extracted, compared (e.g., between timesteps/snapshots), and backpropagated into the DiT.
paper_title: Beyond External Guidance: Unleashing the Semantic Richness Inside Diffusion Transformers for Improved Training
paper_authors: Lingchen Sun, Rongyuan Wu, Zhengqiang Zhang, Ruibin Li, Yujing Sun
